summary: Tested new 'Daftar dengan Google' button on /register plus AuthCallback plumbing. Backend pytest (5/5 pass) uses mocked emergent OAuth to prove new google email creates a student/auth_provider=google user with a 7-day session cookie, and pre-existing email is NOT duplicated. Invalid session_id returns 401 (public HTTP + method-level). /login email/password no regression. Frontend Playwright confirms register-google-button + divider visible on desktop 1920x1080 and mobile 390x844 without overflow; clicking it fires navigation to https://auth.emergentagent.com/?redirect=<encoded window.location.origin + /dashboard> with NO hardcoded fallback. /dashboard#session_id=INVALID triggers AuthCallback synchronously via useLocation().hash, POSTs /api/auth/google/session, gets 401, then redirects to /login. /login page still shows Google button. Real human Google account interaction not executable in sandbox and not attempted per instructions.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py uses synchronous `requests.get(EMERGENT_AUTH_URL, ...)` inside async endpoint. It blocks the event loop for up to 30s. Consider httpx.AsyncClient for the provider call.

google_session inserts a new user_sessions doc every callback with no unique index on session_token; repeated retries or callback re-mounts (mitigated on FE by processed ref) could still leave orphan session rows. Consider upsert on session_token or a TTL index bound to expires_at.
server.py is 5381 lines — well over the 700-line guideline. Should be split into routers/modules (auth, admin, disbursements, etc.).
on_event startup/shutdown is deprecated; migrate to FastAPI lifespan handlers.
test_credentials: supri@baznasbazisdki.id/MdjSuper2026! (verified working). No Google identities stored.
seed_data_creation: None persistent. Test users test_gauth_*@example.com and test_gdup_*@example.com are created and deleted within a single asyncio.run scenario in the mocked test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Real Google OAuth (auth.emergentagent.com) requires human interaction and is not attempted from the sandbox; backend behaviour covered via mocked emergentagent provider response. If you re-run tests, use `python -m pytest backend/tests/test_google_register.py -p xdist -n 0` — motor client is bound to the first asyncio.run loop so scenario methods intentionally consolidate DB ops inside one asyncio.run.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Register Google button uses dynamic window.location.origin, backend rejects invalid session with 401 without persisting user/session, and AuthCallback correctly detects session_id in useLocation().hash before ProtectedRoute mounts.
